question: Should OpenClaw adopt guarded opt-in replay of trusted local installed-package edits and maintain the exact legacy content-inventory exception policy?
rationale: Source and dependency review support the implementation mechanics, but accepting local packaged edits as a supported update workflow and carrying historical package exceptions are long-term product, security, and support choices.

options.title: Approve after clean integration
options.body: Keep preservation by default and guarded opt-in replay after resolving current-main conflicts and refreshing exact-head proof.

options.title: Preserve recovery bundles only
options.body: Keep capture and diagnostics but remove updater-managed replay so users restore files outside the updater.

options.title: Decline package override support
options.body: Close or redesign the PR if local edits to installed package artifacts should remain unsupported.

recommendation.title: Approve after clean integration
recommendation.body: Keep preservation by default and guarded opt-in replay after resolving current-main conflicts and refreshing exact-head proof.
